how_intro: An agent asks. Your home checks the mandate. Then it answers allow, ask or deny – and writes it down.
how_block_household_body: The people who live there. They write the mandate.
how_block_agent_body: Any AI that wants to do something – a voice assistant, an energy app.
how_block_device_body: A light, a lock, a heater. Grouped into {count} categories.
how_block_action_body: What the agent wants: turn on, open, set to 21 °C.
how_block_decision_body: The answer to one request: allow, ask or deny.
how_path_sub: The agent never talks to the device directly. Everything goes through the home guard.
how_node_log_sub: Every request and decision is recorded – also refused ones.
how_path_allow: The guard finds a matching rule and passes the command on right away.
how_path_ask: The guard sends a question to Alex’s phone. Only after “Approve” does the door open. No answer within 2 minutes means no.
how_path_deny: No rule allows it, or a rule forbids it. The device never receives a command.
how_views_sub: The same rules – once as sentences for people, once as JSON for machines. Both say exactly the same.
how_plain_read_all: May read the state of every device
how_plain_lights: May turn lights on, off and dim them
how_plain_climate: May set the temperature up to 22 °C
how_plain_locks: May unlock and open doors if Alex confirms within 2 min
how_plain_no_cameras: May not use cameras – not even look
how_rule_1_body: If no rule fits, the answer is deny.
how_rule_2_body: Order doesn’t matter. deny beats ask, ask beats allow.
how_rule_3_body: An allow only counts if every matching allow rule names them and carries allow_critical. Otherwise allow becomes ask: a person must confirm.
how_rule_4_body: If nobody confirms an ask in time, the answer is deny.
how_rule_5_body: The guard decides, not the agent – the agent can only ask. Every decision is recorded in the log.
how_crit_body: A plain allow is never enough for these. Only a rule that names them and carries allow_critical lets them through without asking – otherwise a person must confirm.
how_crit_note: Your home can also mark single devices as critical, for example a switch that drives a door opener.
how_log_title: The log works like a tachograph
how_log_sub: Each entry contains the fingerprint (SHA-256 hash) of the entry before it. If someone changes an old entry, its fingerprint changes – and the next entry no longer matches.
how_log_ok_body: Every fingerprint matches the entry before it.
how_log_bad_body: Entry 2 was edited, so its fingerprint changed. The fingerprint stored in entry 3 no longer matches – the check fails at entry 3.
how_log_limits: The chain is not signed: whoever can rewrite the whole log can also recompute every fingerprint. It becomes evidence together with a copy or a signed checkpoint kept outside the log.
how_log_tech_text: Digest of an entry: "sha256:" + hex(SHA-256(JCS(entry))), over the complete entry including prev. The first entry has prev null. Exchange format: JSON Lines.
